On Fri, May 28, 2027 at 8:22 AM Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Folks — forwarding Atlas Health's report. Initial read: spikes line up with a proxy keepalive reset in our logs and a burst of chunked-frame backpressure.

Joined bridge; we've collected the serving-side traces. Quick notes:
- We see a pattern of stalled token flushes at the runtime boundary where the kernel send queue length jumps and then a FIN/ACK follows.
- Chunked frames from the model host are being aggregated by the edge proxy (thirdparty-proxy@edgeops.io) which appears to hold for ~5–8s before releasing.
- Error rates (5xx) spike by 2.1x during the window; median token latency doubles for requests with long context.

Hypothesis: proxy buffering + intermittent socket reset under burst causes perceived "silent chunks". Plan: 1) Ask Atlas to route a small percentage of traffic to a proxy-bypass; 2) we push a config to reduce proxy aggregation to immediate flush for Atlas routes.

Will follow up in 30m with concrete mitigation timeline.

Vanessa Ortiz
